lede: Educational one-minute videos for Web3 founders and growth leads. Each one teaches a single fix around conversion, X outreach, KOLs, reply strategy and sales calls. They are the problems our service solves, taught without pitching it.

scripts.hook: Getting leads but not customers? The problem usually isn't your product. It's one of three things.
body:
One. You're talking to the wrong people.

Who you are contacting does not need the service you offer, or the product you built.

But who does?

Everything hinges on this question.

Who is your ideal customer, or "ICP"?

To talk to the people most likely to need your service or product, we need to make a list of assumptions.

This can be who they are their interests, their motivations, their needs & wants...or
where we can find them, social platforms they use, profiles they follow, and more.

A lead who doesn't match these assumptions will never convert, no matter how good your follow-up is.

Two. You're too slow.

A lead is warmest the minute they raise their hand. If your team replies the next day, someone else already did.

This is why tracking "indicators" is so important. An indicator is basically identifying people we believe to match our assumptions.

Let's say you are a banking solution for digital nomads or frequent travellers.

Every time someone follows your competition, being other cross-border banking solutions, that would be an example of an indicator that they are showing interest in this niche.

Three. You stop after one message.

Most deals take several conversations.

Let's say you took the time to curate your ICP list, determined that your best fit customers are on X, write customized DMs to each person, and get no responses.

Those leads are not dead, they just didn't engage.

Most of your conversion issues would be solved by ensuring you have a follow-up sequence and a convincing pitch.

Sending a message thats just "following up" or "checking in" does not count. You need to be adding value, not creating work.
scripts.bodyOst: 1 WRONG PEOPLE · 2 TOO SLOW · 3 ONE TOUCH
scripts.reward:
So fix the list, fix the speed, and build a real follow-up sequence.

Want to learn how this can apply to you? Get your free 90-day growth plan today.
alts: Your lead problem is probably a follow-up problem.
More leads won't fix a funnel that doesn't convert.

scripts.t: Your KOL campaign got views, not users
scripts.hook:
You paid a KOL or influencer, got two hundred thousand impressions and almost no new users.

Here's what went wrong.
body:
The audience those influencers had didn't match the audience you wanted to reach.

Before confirming to work with any influencer, check that their followers are people who need your services or product.

If you are trying to narrow down an initial KOL or influencer list, look at the overlap between your audience and their total audience across all your options.

Second, there was no reason to act.

A post that says "check this out" creates awareness, not users. Give one clear offer and one clear next step.

Third, you couldn't measure conversions.

Without a unique link, code or embedded pixel per creator, you don't know who drove results, so you can't double down on what worked.
scripts.reward: Want to see what this looks like in practice for you? Get your free 90-day growth plan today
alts: Most KOL campaigns are paying for impressions, not customers.
Before you pay another influencer, check these three things.

scripts.t: The cold DM structure that gets replies
scripts.hook:
Most cold DMs get ignored because they are about you, not them.

Here's the structure that actually gets replies.
body:
For the first line, say something like

"Hey [Jane], saw you mentioned working on a product launch for your AI startup. Here is a video on how I tie social engagements directly to your app sign-ups.

[send another X post link]

For the second message:

"Hey [Jane], saw you mentioned working on a product launch for your AI startup. Here is a video on how I tie social engagements directly to your app sign-ups.

[send another X post link]"
Line three: an easy question. Not a calendar link. Something they can answer in five seconds, like "Is growing this a focus for you this quarter?"
Keep it short. No decks, no links, no paragraphs in the first message.
scripts.bodyOst: WHY THEM → ONE OUTCOME → EASY QUESTION
scripts.reward: Specific, short, and easy to answer. On one of our campaigns this structure got about a one-in-four reply rate. Use it on your next ten DMs and compare.
scripts.verify: "One-in-four reply rate" is the Sai benchmark (25%) from the call. Confirm the number and that you can reference it before filming.
alts: Your cold DM is too long. Here's the three-line version.
Stop sending calendar links in your first DM.

scripts.t: Brand or customers? Pick one per campaign
scripts.hook: Before you spend another dollar marketing on X, answer one question: is this campaign for brand, or for customers?
body: Brand campaigns are about attention and trust. You measure reach, community growth, and whether people in your space know your name. Your marketing team and thought leadership drive it.
Acquisition campaigns are about users. You measure signups, deposits, and what each customer costs. They need a clear call to action, an offer, and someone following up on every lead.
When you mix the two, you get content that's too soft to convert and too salesy to build trust. And you can't tell if it worked.
scripts.reward: So label every campaign with one goal and one number before it launches. That single decision tells you who runs it, what to post, and how to judge it.
alts: Most marketing fails because nobody decided what it was for.
Your X strategy is trying to do two jobs at once.

scripts.t: You don't know your cost per customer
scripts.hook: Ask most Web3 founders what it costs to acquire one user, and you'll get a guess.
scripts.hookOst: WHAT DOES ONE USER COST YOU?
body: Here's why. Your on-chain data shows what users do. Your CRM shows how you reached them. Nothing connects the two.
So you can't see which channel brought your best users, the ones who actually trade, deposit, or stay.
The fix is simple. Give every channel, creator, and campaign its own link or referral code. Track each user from first touch to first on-chain action. Review it every week.
scripts.reward: Once you know what a real user costs from each channel, your budget stops being a debate. It becomes math. Spend more where it's cheap, cut where it isn't.
alts: If you can't connect on-chain data to your pipeline, you're guessing.
Your best channel might be the one you're about to cut.

scripts.hook: The most underrated growth channel on X isn't posting. It's replying.
body: The biggest accounts in your niche already have your customers' attention. A sharp reply under their post puts you in front of that audience, with no ad spend.
Here's how to do it. Pick twenty to thirty accounts your ideal customers follow. Reply early, while the post is still climbing.
And add something real: a data point, a contrarian take, a lesson from experience. "Great post" does nothing.
Then do it every day. Consistency is what turns replies into recognition.
scripts.bodyOst: 20–30 ACCOUNTS · REPLY EARLY · ADD VALUE · DAILY
scripts.reward: Do this for a month and something changes. When you send a DM, people already know your name. That's when outreach gets easy.
alts: You don't need more followers. You need better replies.
Here's how to borrow a big account's audience for free.

scripts.t: How to choose the right KOLs
scripts.hook: Follower count is the worst way to choose an influencer. Here's what to look at instead.
body: First, engagement. Open their last ten posts. Are real people replying with real questions, or is it bots and emojis?
Second, audience fit. Click into who follows and engages with them. Do those people look like your customers?
Third, track record. Have they driven signups or volume for projects like yours? Ask for results, not a rate card.
And start small. One paid test post before you sign a package.
scripts.bodyOst: ENGAGEMENT · FIT · TRACK RECORD · TEST FIRST
scripts.reward: A creator with twenty thousand of the right followers will beat one with five hundred thousand of the wrong ones. Pay for proof, then scale what works.
alts: Three checks before you pay any crypto influencer.
Why the smaller KOL usually wins.

scripts.hook: If your product doesn't convert with a hundred users, a big marketing push won't save it.
body: Here's the order we recommend.
Phase one: find where people drop off. Look at every step from first visit to first action and find the biggest leak.
Phase two: talk to people directly. Outreach and one-on-one conversations show you the real objections faster than any dashboard.
Phase three: only once a known share of people convert do you pour in influencers and paid traffic.
scripts.bodyOst: 1 FIND THE LEAK · 2 TALK TO USERS · 3 THEN SCALE
scripts.reward: Traffic makes whatever's already true louder. Make sure it's good news before you turn up the volume.
alts: The most expensive mistake in growth: scaling too early.
Fix conversion before you buy attention.

scripts.t: Your first sales call: stop talking
scripts.hook: If you're doing most of the talking on a sales call, you're losing the deal.
body: Open by framing the call. Tell them you've prepared a few questions and what they'll get by the end.
Then ask them to describe their ideal customer in their own words. Ask what they've already tried, and what's actually worked.
Find out what they want most: brand awareness, or more customers. That tells you which problem to solve.
Only then show a demo. Five minutes, focused on the outcome they just described.
scripts.reward: And before you hang up, book the next meeting while you're both still on the call. The best calls end with them explaining their problem better than you could.
alts: The best salespeople barely talk on the first call.
Your demo is too long. Here's the five-minute version.

scripts.t: One message for everyone reaches no one
scripts.hook: If you're sending the same message to a trader, a founder, and a fund, you're losing all three.
body: Each persona cares about something different. A trader cares about fees, execution, and rewards. A founder cares about users and distribution. A fund cares about traction.
So start by naming your two or three core personas. For each one, write down the problem they feel most.
Then write a separate opener for each, using their words, not yours. Track replies by persona so you can see which group responds.
scripts.reward: Same product, three messages. Your reply rate goes up because every person reads something that sounds like it was written for them, because it was.
alts: Who is your outreach actually written for?
Why generic outreach gets generic results.

scripts.t: Seven ways to get customers. Pick one.
scripts.hook: There are seven main ways to get customers. Most early teams try all seven and do none of them well.
body: Here they are: direct outreach, partnerships, influencers and creator content, paid ads, search and AI search, events, and outsourced business development.
If you're early and budget is tight, start with direct outreach and partnerships. They're cheap, and every conversation teaches you something.
Once you know which message converts, add one amplifier, like creators or ads, to push that message further.
scripts.bodyOst: OUTREACH · PARTNERS · CREATORS · ADS · SEARCH · EVENTS · BD
scripts.reward: One channel done well beats seven done halfway. Get one working, measure it, then add the next.
alts: Your growth problem might be doing too much.
Where should an early-stage team find its first customers?

scripts.t: Cold outreach on X without getting flagged
scripts.hook: Cold outreach on X can get your account restricted. Here's how to do it safely.
body: First, warm up the account. Complete profile, real posting history, real engagement before you send a single DM.
Second, ramp slowly. Start with a small number of messages a day and increase gradually. Sudden spikes are what trip the filters.
Third, personalize. Identical messages get flagged, and irrelevant ones get reported.
Fourth, watch your numbers. If replies drop or reports rise, slow down and fix the targeting.
scripts.bodyOst: WARM UP · RAMP SLOWLY · PERSONALIZE · MONITOR
scripts.reward: Safe outreach is slower and more targeted, and that's exactly why it converts better. We've run client accounts for three months straight without a single flag.
scripts.verify: "Three months without a flag" is from the call. Confirm it's still true for every client account before saying it on camera.
alts: The fastest way to lose your X account: bad outreach.
How to scale DMs on X without getting restricted.
